page: Amazon Web Services r8id.24xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with 96 vCPUs and 48 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor operating at 3.9 GHz. The processor includes a 480 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). The instance is equipped with 768.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 7 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. It also bundles 5700 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage and delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 40 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates a strong contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. While single-core stress-ng CPU performance falls into the average category, multi-core performance is strong, and the overall PassMark CPU score ranks in the top tier. Memory performance is characterized by top-tier read-only bandwidth for both small and large blocks, though the PassMark memory score itself is average. The hardware demonstrates top-tier capabilities in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, database operations, and Redis SET operations, which reached 172.71 million operations per second. For machine learning workloads, the Intel AMX instructions assist in achieving top-tier LLM inference prompt processing speeds for 7B and 70B models, though text generation speeds for larger models remain in the average tier.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the r8id.24xlarge offers high resource density by combining a large memory footprint with fast DDR5 speeds and high-capacity local NVMe SSD storage. This integration reduces the need for external storage attachments for data-intensive operations. The instance is suited for memory-intensive workloads, large-scale database deployments, Redis caching layers, multi-threaded data processing, and CPU-based LLM inference prompt processing.
